name: Nomad List (now Nomads.com)
tagline: City data and a paid community for remote workers choosing where to live
summary: Nomad List ranks cities for remote workers on cost of living, internet speed, weather and safety, and sells membership to a community of nomads. Pieter Levels started it in 2014 as a crowdsourced spreadsheet and has run it mostly alone ever since. It was rebranded to Nomads.com in 2024.
origin: In 2014 Levels was running out of money and set himself a challenge to launch 12 startups in 12 months. He tweeted a public Google Spreadsheet asking people to add data on cities good for remote work, and it filled up quickly. He then turned the sheet into a website, which became Nomad List.
howItMakesMoney: Paid membership unlocks the community (chat, meetups, dating and member features) and full city data. The membership price and billing model have changed many times; exact current prices aren't included here because none could be confirmed from a primary source. Sponsorships and ads have also contributed.
growth: The crowdsourced spreadsheet validated demand before any code was written, and contributors became the first audience.
SEO: thousands of city and comparison pages ('cost of living in X') bring in steady organic search traffic.
Open-startup transparency: Levels published live revenue and user dashboards from 2018, which fed press coverage and his own following.
Conversion experiments: he reported sign-ups up 26% after adding Stripe Checkout and ran randomized tests of the benefits shown in the sign-up modal.
Combined with Remote OK, he reported $83,333+/mo (a $1M/yr run rate) in May 2019 with 0 ad budget and 0 funding.
moat: More than a decade of crowdsourced city data and reviews, strong SEO rankings, and a paid community with network effects are hard to replicate quickly.
risks: Revenue swings with travel trends (COVID hit it hard) and with the remote-work cycle. The product depends on one founder who now spreads his attention across many projects.

timeline.event: Tweets a crowdsourced Google Sheet of nomad-friendly cities during the 12 startups in 12 months challenge, then launches the site
Becomes an Open Startup with public revenue and user stats
Nomad List + Remote OK pass $83,333/mo ($1M/yr run rate) with 1 VPS and no funding
Levels reports ~$700k/yr across his one-person business, mostly Nomad List and Remote OK
Reports ~$61k/month from Nomad List in a record portfolio month

lessons: Validate with a spreadsheet before writing code: a public sheet can prove demand in a day.
Programmatic data pages (one per city, one per comparison) compound SEO for years.
Monetize the community, not just the data. Public data brings people in and membership pays the bills.
Keep infrastructure tiny. Levels reported running both sites from 1 VPS at ~$5.5k/mo total costs in 2019.

rebuild.idea: A 'where to live' data site plus paid community for remote-working families: school options, pediatric care, kid-friendly neighborhoods and visa rules for dependents, city by city.
rebuild.why: Nomad-focused sites are built around single travellers. Families relocating for remote work have different, higher-stakes data needs and are willing to pay more.
mvp: Start a public Google Sheet of 30 cities with columns for international schools, fees and pediatric hospitals, and post it in remote-family Facebook groups and subreddits.
Interview 10 families who moved abroad and write 5 in-depth city guides from those interviews.
Ship a static site from the sheet with one page per city.
Sell a $49/year membership that includes a private chat and monthly city deep-dive calls.
rebuild.fit: Parents who have relocated abroad and can seed the community from lived experience
